title: International Court of Justice orders Azerbaijan to keep the Lachin Corridor open
body:
On 22 February 2023 the International Court of Justice issued an Order on Armenia's request for provisional measures in the case concerning the Application of the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (Armenia v. Azerbaijan). The Court's press release is numbered 2023/10. The request came while the Lachin Corridor, the only road linking Armenia and Nagorno-Karabakh, had been obstructed since 12 December 2022.

The Court indicated a single provisional measure. Pending a final decision in the case, Azerbaijan must take all measures at its disposal to ensure unimpeded movement of persons, vehicles and cargo along the Lachin Corridor in both directions. The press release describes provisional measures as having binding effect.

The Order was adopted by thirteen votes to two. In favour were President Joan Donoghue, Vice-President Kirill Gevorgian, and Judges Tomka, Abraham, Bennouna, Xue, Robinson, Salam, Iwasawa, Nolte, Charlesworth and Brant, together with Judge ad hoc Daudet. Judge Yusuf and Judge ad hoc Keith voted against, and both appended declarations to the Order. The press release refers readers to earlier ICJ press releases in the proceedings and to a separate summary of the Order's reasoning.
